lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Today's refresher: Slurm accounting and associations.
Where does sacct find jobs that left the queue long ago? And why does Slurm reject a job for an invalid account?
slurmctld sends a record of every job to slurmdbd, the accounting daemon, which keeps them in a database, such as MariaDB.
sacct reads the records back, even for jobs that finished long ago.
The database also holds the associations. An association ties a user to an account, on a cluster.
Accounts form a tree under root, and one user can belong to several of them.
Associations carry limits, like a cap on running jobs, or on CPUs for a whole account.
A cap on an account covers everything below it, and per-user caps like MaxJobs pass down to its users.
sacctmgr manages all of it: accounts, users, coordinators and their limits.
But limits only bite with enforcement. One setting in slurm.conf rejects jobs without an association, and applies the limits.
So: slurmdbd keeps the records, associations link users to accounts and carry limits, and enforcement makes them count.
Next up: episode five, Model your site. See you there!
